note: The fleet's glaeda-gh pacing, installed by glaeda-mini-setup (every profile) to ~/.local/share/glaeda/gh-daemon.json, where the daemon reads it every tick. default applies on every host; hosts[NAME] (NAME is ~/.config/glaeda/update.json host, else the short hostname) is laid over it, and ~/.config/glaeda/gh-daemon.json over both. Every daemon on the shared account polls on one REST quota, so the restShare values here sum to at most maxRestShare (a test checks it): a host not named gets 0 and reads PRs and runs over GraphQL only (its one REST read is the cap's exemption, a failed attempt's job list, once per attempt). Measured 2026-10-27, last hour per daemon: one host 2101 counted REST requests, one 546, one 155, every other host 0. Measured 2026-10-30, with the shared REST quota run out again while GraphQL sat about 90% unused: cosmic-gray's daemon 1160 counted REST requests in the hour (of its 1250 cap), huge-blue's 411 (of 500), so the daemons were a third of the account's REST spend that gh, landers and reruns can only make over REST. The shares now sum to 0.1 (500 an hour): a daemon's PR and run reads go to GraphQL, 15 PRs a query, and REST stays for what only REST can read.
floorsNote: default.floors.graphql: every daemon stops its GraphQL reads below 1000 left on the shared login (lean below 1500), keeping that much of each hour for lands: merges and the lane-gh broker's gate reads. Measured 2026-11-04: the account's /graphql counter ran to 0 minutes before each :26 reset at about 96 points a minute across the fleet, and lane-VM lands were refused for it.
alarmsNote: alarms.pool watches the account-wide REST pool, so one host sends it (cosmic-gray); alarms.share, on by default, watches each daemon's own counted REST over the measured last hour against its restShare cap and names the waiter to shed; a fast 10 minutes under the cap is a log line only (scripts/glaeda-gh share_alarm). Checked 2026-11-15 ~19:55Z: the account's REST window had 1892 of 5000 left 30 minutes in, the daemons' measured hour was cosmic-gray 182 of 300 and huge-blue 148 of 150 (about 7% of the pool together), so the shares stay: raising one would take from gh, landers and reruns, which only REST serves. Measured 2026-11-18 over the last 24 h of share alarms (each host's notices): cosmic-gray 301-312 counted REST an hour on its cap of 300 (17 alarms), huge-blue 151-185 on 150 (19), a host with no share 1-60 on 0 (exempt reads only). Every daemon sits pinned at its cap, so its demand is above the cap and cannot be read past it; the overshoot is only the exempt reads (a failed attempt's job list, up to 35 an hour). A raised cap is spent in full, so the shares stay. The same day the login's pool fell under its 1500 floor in the 25 minutes before its :25 reset in 11 of the 18 hours cosmic-gray's pool alarm logged (under 1000 in 8, down to 402): that is when another daemon REST read takes from gh, landers and reruns, and the only time the share alarm fires now (under floors.rest, naming the one caller to slow); above the floor it is a log line.
